overview.description: Durak Prostoy (Simple Fool) is the archaic and most straightforward version of the Russian card game Durak. Predating the popular 'Podkidnoy' (throw-in) and 'Perevodnoy' (transfer) variants, it simplifies the interaction between players. In Prostoy, an attacker leads a card or a group of cards of the same rank, and the defender must either beat all of them or pick them up. There are no secondary attacks or throwing in of cards once the defense has begun, making for a faster, more linear game focused on card-for-card strength.

history.origins: Prostoy is the original form of Durak that emerged in the 18th century. It was the standard way the game was played until the late 19th century when the 'throw-in' (Podkidnoy) rules were introduced and eventually became the new standard.
timeline: 1700s: Durak Prostoy is documented in Russian royal courts and remote villages alike.
1850s: Modern variations begin to overshadow the Simple version.
Modern: Primarily played as a fast training variant or by children learning the basics of Russian beating games.
history.evolution: The transition from Prostoy to Podkidnoy marked the shift from individual card strength to tactical group collaboration.
history.cultural: Regarded as the 'grandparent' of Russian card games; it represents the simplest expression of the 'Fool' mechanic.

setup.deck: 36-card Russian pack (6, 7, 8, 9, 10, J, Q, K, A).
setup.dealing: Each player is dealt 5 cards, one at a time clockwise. The next card is placed face-up to determine the trump suit; the stock is placed face down on it.

rules.objective: Shed all cards. Do not be the last person remaining with cards.
rules.gameplay:
1. Attacking: One player leads a single card or several cards of the SAME RANK.
2. Defending: The defender must beat all lead cards (higher card of same suit or trump).
3. Outcome: If beaten, the cards are discarded. If not, the defender picks them up.
4. Ending: No more cards can be added to the attack once the defender starts their defense.
keyRules: Only the cards played in the initial lead constitute the attack.
Players replenish their hands only after the defense is completely resolved.
If more than one card is led, they MUST be of the same rank (e.g., two 7s).

strategy.basic: Save your trumps for rounds where the attacker leads multi-card attacks of the same rank.
strategy.intermediate: Hand Management: Since there is no throwing-in, you can safely play high cards early to ensure you have a 'safe' exit once the deck is empty.
strategy.advanced: The Multi-Lead: If you have three of a kind, lead all three at once. This significantly increases the odds that the defender will be forced to pick up cards, given they must respond to all three in one go without the benefit of a sequential defense.
tips: In Prostoy, the attacker has a significant advantage in the lead because they can dictate the exact number of cards the defender must handle.
Count the trumps! Since the game is linear, knowing how many trumps remain is easier and more effective than in complex variations.

difficulty.easy: Fails to lead multiple cards of the same rank; wastes trumps on single-card leads.
difficulty.medium: Leads pairs and triplets; tracks used trumps.
difficulty.hard: Optimal lead selection based on the defender's known discards.

considerations: AI strategy is significantly simpler for Prostoy as there is no need to model potential throw-ins from other players.

trumpConfig.overtakingRule: Higher card of same suit beats lower; any trump beats non-trump.

validPlays.notes: Attacker leads one card, or three (pair plus any third), or five (two pairs plus any fifth or four of rank plus any fifth).
Defender beats each attack card with higher same suit or any trump; unbeaten cards are picked up by defender.

edgeCases.text: Attacker cannot lead more cards than the defender holds.
Holder of trump 6 may exchange it for the face-up trump before stock is exhausted.
Draw when two players remain and both empty their hands on the same turn; previous loser still deals next.
Defender who uses all cards to beat and has no stock drops out; attack passes to player to defender's left.

engine.handRankingSystem: Individual card rank within suit; trump beats non-trump. No composite hand rankings.
engine.deckDescription: A stripped French deck containing 36 cards with four suits (Hearts, Diamonds, Clubs, Spades) and nine ranks per suit (6 through Ace), created by removing cards 2 through 5 from a standard 52-card deck.
engine.suitDescription: Four traditional French suits: Hearts (Cœur), Diamonds (Carreau), Clubs (Trèfle), and Spades (Pique), each represented with standard French card design and distinct color coding for easy suit identification.
engine.rankDescription: Nine ranks per suit starting from 6: 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, Jack (Valet), Queen (Dame), King (Roi), and Ace as the highest card, where each rank has specific value and importance in determining game outcomes.
engine.dealPattern: Clockwise, one card at a time to each player.
